grammar_concept.title: Future with "going to"
grammar_concept.rule: Use "am/is/are + going to + base verb" to talk about plans and intentions already decided before the moment of speaking.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: We use this when we already decided to do something — it's not a spontaneous decision, it's a plan.
grammar_concept.example: I am going to visit my parents next weekend. She is going to start a new job in June.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Eu vou visitar os meus pais no próximo fim de semana. Ela vai começar um trabalho novo em junho.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Falantes de português tendem a esquecer o verbo "to be" (am/is/are), porque em português "vou viajar" não precisa de um verbo auxiliar equivalente: dizem "I going to travel" em vez de "I am going to travel".
grammar_concept.correction: "Going to" precisa sempre do verbo "to be" antes: I am going to / she is going to / they are going to — nunca "I going to" sozinho.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: A dizer a um colega: "We are going to launch the new website next month."

vocabulary.definition_en: to intend to do something in the future
example_sentences: We plan to move to a new apartment next year.
I am going to start the course next week.

vocabulary.definition_en: to change your home to a new place
example_sentences: They are going to move to a bigger city.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: I ___ going to call you tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: Com "I", o verbo "to be" no presente é sempre "am".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Falantes de português tendem a esquecer o verbo "to be" por completo, não só a forma correta.

correct_answer: She is going to start a new job.
distractors: She going to start a new job.
She go to start a new job.
She is go to start a new job.
exercises.explanation: "Going to" precisa do verbo "to be" (is, com "she") antes.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Omitir o "is" é o erro mais comum nesta posição.

correct_answer: to change your home to a new place
exercises.explanation: "Move to" refere-se especificamente a mudar de casa para um novo lugar.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What is Laura going to do next month?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "Next month, Laura is going to move to a new city for her studies."
exercises.transcript: Next month, Laura is going to move to a new city for her studies.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "Next week, Marco is going to start a new course at the university. He is also going to move into a new apartment closer to the campus." What is Marco going to do closer to the campus?
correct_answer: move into a new apartment closer to the campus
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente que ele vai "move into a new apartment closer to the campus".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Nós vamos visitar os meus pais na próxima semana."
correct_answer: We are going to visit my parents next week.
exercises.explanation: Atenção ao verbo "to be" ("are", com "we") antes de "going to" — não pode ser omitido.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Esquecer o "are" é o erro mais comum nesta frase.

steps.content: In natural speech, "going to" is often pronounced "gonna" /ˈɡʌnə/ in casual conversation — you will hear this a lot, but keep writing "going to" in formal contexts.

steps.prompt: Describe 3 plans you have for next month using "going to".
Write 5 sentences about your plans for next year using "going to".
